root_motivation: Make software visible-as-terrain by extracting the per-file topographic primitives from a git repository (elevation = commit density, biome = language, territory = primary author). Phase 0 produces the structured walker JSON that all later rendering passes (SVG mockup, cartographer, A1 print) consume. Until the walker emits faithful primitives, no downstream art can be evaluated.
user_persona: jsy running it against `~/wintermute` (and later other repos) to inspect the JSON output before any rendering exists. Audience is the human eye reading the JSON to sanity-check that the topographic primitives feel right.

unfakeable_metric.name: acceptance_tests_passing
unfakeable_metric.harness_command: cargo test --tests 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok' | wc -l

acceptance_criteria.description: `repo-as-landscape walk --repo <git-dir>` emits a single JSON object on stdout. Top-level: `{"repo": "<absolute path>", "generated_at": "<RFC3339>", "files": [...]}`. Each file entry is `{"path": "<repo-relative>", "language": "<lang>", "commit_count": <u32>, "last_touched": "<RFC3339>", "primary_author": "<name>", "size_bytes": <u64>}`. Exits 0 on success.

Language detection covers at least: Rust (.rs), Python (.py), TypeScript (.ts/.tsx), JavaScript (.js/.jsx), Markdown (.md), JSON (.json), TOML (.toml), Shell (.sh/.bash/.zsh), YAML (.yml/.yaml), HTML (.html), CSS (.css), Go (.go), C (.c/.h), C++ (.cpp/.hpp), Java (.java). Files without a known extension get `"language": "unknown"`.

`commit_count` counts the number of commits touching the file across the full reachable history of HEAD (equivalent to `git log --follow --oneline -- <path> | wc -l`). `last_touched` is the committer date of the most recent such commit.
`primary_author` is the author whose commits touching the file outnumber any other author's commits on it. Ties break by most recent commit. Author identity is the commit author name (not email).
Running against a non-git path exits with code 2 and stderr containing the path and `not a git repository`.
Files matched by `.gitignore` are excluded from the output (we walk the index/HEAD, not the working tree). Untracked files do not appear.
`--summary` flag prints (to stderr) a one-line summary per language: `<lang>: <file-count> files, <total-commits> commits` before the main JSON. Default JSON output on stdout is unaffected.

`--coalesce-below <N>` collapses any directory containing fewer than N tracked files into a single synthetic file entry `{path: "<dir>/.", language: "directory", commit_count: sum_of_children, ...}` so deep trees stay legible.

scope: Walk a git repository's HEAD tree
Per-tracked-file: language detection by extension, commit count via git log, last-touched date, primary author, size
Emit one JSON object to stdout
non_goals: SVG, PNG, or any pixel/vector rendering
Biome color mapping or cartographic styling
Multi-repo aggregation (single --repo per invocation; downstream tools concatenate)
GitHub/GitLab API integration — local git only
Diff/blame intelligence beyond commit-count and author-tally

five_whys_trace.q: Why ship the walker as Phase 0 instead of going straight to the SVG render?
five_whys_trace.a: Because cartographic rendering is taste-laden and iterative — the only way to test if the rendering is right is to have stable, faithful input primitives to feed it. The walker is the contract every later stage depends on.

five_whys_trace.q: Why JSON instead of an in-process Rust struct?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the cartographer step will be a separate process (likely SVG via Typst or Inkscape templating) — and the JSON is also the form a future curator/designer can audit by hand.

five_whys_trace.q: Why include primary_author when this is jsy's personal portrait?
five_whys_trace.a: Because some wintermute repos have contributions from collaborators (or pasted code), and 'territory' on the print is a real signal — knowing where someone else's hand is in the topology matters cartographically.
